body.estimand_functional: \(\mathcal R(P_X)=A_q(P_X)\) on the heterogeneous-observed certified class, where the finite exact-real algorithm of Theorem~\textnormal{thm:finite-exact-aq-reconstruction} enumerates observable nonsingular row minors, nonnegative normalized measurement tables, and all same-\(K\) realizations.

sampling_model.design: Population identification from the exact mass function \(P_X\) on \(\mathcal X=\prod_j\mathcal X_j\); the optional empirical rung observes \(n\) independent heterogeneous response vectors.
sampling_model.units: Independent respondents with common categorical response law \(P_X\) only in the empirical rung.
sampling_model.treatment: There is no designated treatment; the causal target is the latent measurement graph, latent law, and latent DAG Markov-equivalence class.
sampling_model.overlap: Every one of the \(q^K\) latent configurations has positive probability; measurement probabilities may be zero.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: No nuisance is estimated in the population results.  The empirical open question replaces queried observed marginals by cell proportions and must calibrate the resulting adaptive family.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Lee and Gu treat binary latent coordinates with arbitrary observed variables on nondegenerate separable metric spaces under their standing BLCM assumptions, including faithfulness; their Theorem 1 gives the rank and dimension result and their Theorem 2 gives structural identification under its additional graph conditions.

Under completeness, nondegeneracy, two sufficient measurements, and the stated support condition, a mixed-type discrete latent structure and its latent MEC are identified by tensor-rank and discretization arguments.
Three finite latent-class views are generically identifiable up to label swapping when their Kruskal ranks meet the stated inequality.
Population tensor unfoldings constructively identify a \(Q\)-matrix when every latent attribute has at least two pure items.
A measurement graph and latent law can be reconstructed from a mixture oracle under no-twins, maximality, nondegeneracy, and subset conditions.
Binary restricted latent-class \(Q\)-matrices admit checkable strict and generic identifiability criteria.
Observable response restrictions yield calibrated goodness-of-fit tests for a provisional cognitive-diagnosis \(Q\)-matrix.

body.tldr: The headline result is a terminating exact-real algorithm \(A_q\) for \(q\ge3\) latent states and heterogeneous finite responses with \(m_j\ge q\).  A product of local Gram determinants \(c_{a,k,u}=\det(L_{a,k,u}^{\mathsf T}L_{a,k,u})\) certifies full column rank of two rectangular triangular views, exact three-view recovery supplies \(q^K\) anonymous components, and the observable equality lattice aligns them with \(K\) categorical coordinates and a latent MEC.  The two-view rank also forces every finite latent measurement representation to have at least \(q^K\) joint states and gives \(K_{\min}(P_X)=K\).  In the equal-\(q\) case the original determinant product remains an exact if-and-only-if frontier.  That converse cannot extend to all larger alphabets: a strictly positive \(q=3\) witness has a singular earlier local table but a full-rank rectangular view.  The dense ternary no-pure-child witness remains an exact regression fixture, and the sole open rung is finite-sample multiplicity calibration for a \(\texttt{cdmTools}\)-style diagnostic.

project_justification.gap: Binary double triangularity uses scalar contrasts, while categorical and heterogeneous responses require local column-rank certificates.  Generic Kruskal theory neither identifies the failing predecessor context nor aligns \(q^K\) anonymous mixture labels with \(K\) coordinates and a latent MEC.  A further subtlety is that local-rank necessity fails when a later observed alphabet is larger than \(q\), so an honest heterogeneous theorem must distinguish a sufficient Gram certificate from the exact equal-alphabet frontier.
project_justification.niche: The project gives an explicit rectangular certificate \(c_{a,k,u}=\det(L_{a,k,u}^{\mathsf T}L_{a,k,u})=\sum_R\det(L_{a,k,u}[R,:])^2\), an embedded positive perturbation proving open-dense/full-measure nonvanishing, and observable \(q^K\)-row minors that support exact simultaneous diagonalization without pure children or positive measurement-cell assumptions.
project_justification.fill: The note delivers the finite exact algorithm \(A_q\), the rectangular certificate implication and sharp equal-\(q\) determinant corollary, a counterexample to the impossible heterogeneous converse, an arbitrary finite-latent-state lower bound, intrinsic coordinate dimension, exact same-\(K\) quotient identification, coordinate alignment, and the dense \(q=3\) no-pure-child regression fixture.

body.related_work: Lee and Gu (2026) study binary latent coordinates with arbitrary observed variables on nondegenerate separable metric spaces under their standing BLCM assumptions, including faithfulness.  The reduced-assumption binary-response rank class used here is a strengthening proved directly; the published Theorem 1 transfers only on its faithful intersection.  The binary-response identification comparator is a subclass of their Theorem 2 domain.  For \(q\ge3\), the present result is a categorical-latent analogue with an additional local Gram-rank certificate, not an inclusion transfer.  Chen et al. (2025) obtain mixed-type recovery through completeness and two sufficient measurements.  Their unchanged published class and the full heterogeneous finite-observed certified class are incomparable: the first noncontainment is witnessed by the equal-alphabet dense ternary member, whose observed and latent supports both have size three and therefore fail Chen et al.'s strict larger-support requirement, while the reverse noncontainment is witnessed by Chen-class members with continuous measurements, which cannot belong to the finite-observed certified class.  The support-cardinality argument is confined to the equal-alphabet witness; heterogeneous certified members may overlap Chen's class without altering either noncontainment.  Allman, Matias, and Rhodes (2009) give generic latent-class uniqueness under Kruskal inequalities; here certified full-rank row minors and third-view separation yield exact uniqueness, after which the equality lattice supplies the missing coordinate product, measurement adjacency, and latent MEC.  Gu (2026) gives constructive unfolding queries under pure-item conditions, and Kivva et al. (2021) recover structure from a mixture oracle; \(A_q\) instead enumerates exact row minors, coordinate partitions, nonnegative normalized measurement tables, and latent DAGs directly from \(P_X\).  Gu and Xu (2021) and Gu et al. (2018) motivate the software consumer and its still-open calibrated empirical layer.
body.interpretation: For heterogeneous responses, \(\Delta_{\mathrm{DT}}\neq0\) is a finite, checkable sufficient certificate, not a necessary characterization of global view rank.  The exact frontier survives when the selected alphabets all have size \(q\), where \(c_{a,k,u}=d_{a,k,u}^2\) and \(\Delta_a=\det(M_a)^2\).  Larger downstream alphabets can encode predecessor context and compensate for a singular earlier local table; the explicit positive construction with \(m_{s(a,1)}=3\) and \(m_{s(a,2)}=9\) proves this is a structural phenomenon rather than a boundary artifact.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The population algorithm assumes exact access to \(P_X\) and exact-real equality, rank, discriminant, and conditional-independence queries.  It permits zero measurement cells and requires positivity only of latent weights.  Finite-sample soundness cannot be obtained by arbitrary thresholding near intersecting rank varieties; multiplicity-calibrated testing under a declared separation margin is the sole remaining open question.
body.honest_scope: For \(q\ge3\) and finite observed alphabets \(m_j\ge q\), the proved population results are rectangular certificate sufficiency, open-dense/full-measure genericity, exact three-view and coordinate-aligned quotient identification, the \(q^K\) lower bound for every finite latent measurement representation, \(K_{\min}(P_X)=K\), and a terminating sound-and-complete exact algorithm over the maximal same-\(K\) comparison domain.  The determinant product is necessary and sufficient only when every selected alphabet has size \(q\); the note explicitly disproves the unrestricted heterogeneous converse.  The existing dense \(q=3,K=3,J=8\) no-pure-child witness remains within the equal-alphabet subfamily.  Unequal latent-coordinate cardinalities, observed alphabets smaller than \(q\), observed-to-observed edges, orientation beyond the latent MEC, and the finite-sample calibration problem stated in Open-ended Question 2 are outside the proved scope.
